newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Veltroni says confident on DPEF talks.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Veltroni says confident on DPEF talks.

text.p: Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni said the Italian government was looking with confidence to talks with trade unions and employers at 1500 GMT on the government's three-year economic targets for 1998-2000.

Veltroni spoke to reporters after morning talks with parliamentary leaders of parties allied to the centre-left government and preparatory meetings with leaders of the main union confederations and the business group Confindustria.
"The morning went very well. At the end of the morning appreciation prevailed over problems. That allows us to look forward to the meeting at five o'clock (1500 GMT) with confidence."

The economic targets, contained in a document known as the DPEF, will be a vital indicator of how Italy intends to sustain criteria laid down for a single European currency, especially on the budget deficit.

Union sources say the DPEF, which the cabinet is due to approve on Friday, sets a 2.8 percent deficit-GDP ratio for 1998, when official sources say the government intends to make deficit cuts of 25 trillion lire.
Controversy has raged over how much of this should come from spending cuts, including pensions and welfare spending.
Trade unions and the Communist Refoundation party, which ensures the government's parliamentary majority, are opposed to deep cuts.
Newspapers have reported that two-thirds of the 1998 deficit reductions would come from spending cuts and one-third from extra revenue but political sources on Thursday said the mix would be 60-40.
"The ratio between cuts and new revenues will be 60-40," the Greens party Senate (upper house) leader, Maurizio Pieroni, said after Thursday morning's meeting.
Veltroni said that after the morning talks the conditions were right "for serious negotiations on the welfare state".
